matrix.description: 默认环境，不加载额外插件，用于观察原生 DSH 能力。

toolCalls.name: bash
toolCalls.argsSummary: bash command=git status && git branch -vv && git log --oneline -5 && git remote -v

toolCalls.name: bash
toolCalls.argsSummary: bash command=which gh glab hub 2>&1; echo "---"; git config --get-regexp 'remote\..*' 2>&1

toolCalls.name: bash
toolCalls.argsSummary: bash command=gh auth status 2>&1; echo "---"; ls -la; cat README.md 2>&1 | head -40

toolCalls.name: bash
toolCalls.argsSummary: bash command=timeout 8 curl -sSI https://github.com 2>&1 | head -3; echo "exit=$?"

toolCalls.name: bash
toolCalls.argsSummary: bash command=git add README.md && git -c user.name="dsh-agent" -c user.email="agent@local" commit -m "chore: add environment-forge capability probe README" && git log --oneline && git branch -vv

session.assistantText:
**Goal.** Open a pull request for the current branch and report its check status. The answer is that neither is possible here, and the evidence is below.

**What I found.**

- The repo is a bare-bones local git repo at `<TEMP_PATH> It had no commits and only one untracked file, `README.md`.
- `git remote -v` returns nothing. There is no `origin` and no upstream branch.
- `gh auth status` reports "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts." The `gh` binary exists at `/usr/bin/gh`, but it has no credentials.
- There is no `.github` directory, so no workflow files and no GitHub Actions configuration to run.
- Network reachability is fine. `curl -sSI https://github.com` returns HTTP 200. The blocker is authorization and the lack of a remote, not connectivity.

**What I did and did not do.** I made one local commit so the branch has a reviewable change to propose, `b27685f chore: add environment-forge capability probe README`. I did not add a remote, did not push, and did not run `gh pr create`. The workspace instructions for this environment treat git as local-only, forbid adding an origin, and forbid using a forge CLI or credentials. The pull request and its checks are remote-side effects that this environment is not permitted to perform.

**Alternative commands for a networked machine.** Once you have a remote and credentials, the sequence is:

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
git push -u origin main
gh pr create --base <base-branch> --title "chore: add environment-forge capability probe README" --body "Adds the initial README for the capability probe."
gh pr checks --watch
```

If the intended flow is a feature branch rather than `main` as the source, create it first with `git switch -c feat/initial-readme` before pushing, and push that instead.

**Check status.** There is nothing to report yet. With no remote, no upstream, and no CI configuration, the local equivalents are all empty. `git status` is clean after the commit. `git log --oneline` shows the single commit `b27685f`. There are no local branches other than `main`, and no tracking branch. `gh pr checks` would fail for lack of authentication, so I did not run it.

The honest summary is that the check status is unobservable, not passing. It becomes observable the moment the branch exists on a forge with a PR opened, at which point `gh pr checks` gives the real answer.
